union.summary: Single-dash setext headings (`Heading\n-`) and any paragraph followed by a lone `-`/`*`/`+` line now render as a paragraph plus an empty list item — the guard is not scoped to the nested/indented case it was written for
union.evidence:
`const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1;` in the replaced `lheading`, combined with `wrappedList`'s condition (`silent && state.parentType === 'paragraph' && isEmptyBulletLine(state, startLine)`), applies at ANY indent and in ANY paragraph context — nothing requires the dash line to be indented deeper than the paragraph (i.e. to actually be a nested child). Trace `Heading -` at top level: blkIndent=0, sCount[1]=0 >= 0, marker `-`, end-of-line → isEmptyBulletLine true → paragraph terminates → the stock `list` rule runs non-silently (its empty-item guard only applies when `silent && parentType==='paragraph'`) and emits `
`. Result: `

Heading

` where CommonMark, GitHub and the previous notes behavior all give `

Heading

`. The same path fires for `foo *` and `foo +` (previously lazy-continuation text), because `isEmptyBulletLine` accepts `*` and `+` even though `lheading` never claimed them. docs/design/notes/notes.md added in this diff asserts "ordinary setext headings still render", which is only true for `---`/`=`; and the plugin's own TODO listed a "top-level lone dash" test (docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-todo.md) that was never added, so this regression is uncovered. Scoping the relaxation to `state.sCount[line] > state.blkIndent` (a genuinely nested bullet) would fix the target case without breaking existing single-dash setext content.

union.summary: `getRuleFn` reads markdown-it's private `__rules__` and throws at module-import time, so a dependency change takes down the whole notes preview module instead of degrading
union.evidence: `const rule = ruler.__rules__.find((r) => r.name === name); if (!rule) throw new Error(...)`. `getRuleFn` is called from `listEmptyBulletPlugin`, which `preview.ts` invokes at module top level (`md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)`). If a markdown-it upgrade renames/reshapes the private `__rules__` registry, `ruler.__rules__` is `undefined` and `.find` throws a TypeError (or the `Error` throws) during module evaluation of `preview.ts`, breaking every import of the notes preview rather than just losing the empty-bullet behavior. A try/catch that falls back to leaving `list` unwrapped would keep the failure local.

union.summary: `Ruler.at('list', ...)` restores a hardcoded `alt` chain instead of the rule's current one, silently dropping any alt membership added by plugins registered earlier
union.evidence: `md.block.ruler.at('list', wrappedList, { alt: ['paragraph', 'reference', 'blockquote'] });` — `Ruler.at` overwrites `alt` with `options.alt || []`, and the values here are copied from stock markdown-it. In `preview.ts` this plugin is registered AFTER `taskLists`, `katexPlugin` and `detailsPlugin`; if any of those (or a future plugin) added its own block name to `list`'s alt chain so that a list terminates it, that membership is discarded here and `list` stops terminating that construct. The code already reaches into `__rules__` in `getRuleFn`, so it could read and pass back the existing `alt` array instead of hardcoding it.

union.summary: `isEmptyBulletLine` omits the `sCount - blkIndent >= 4` code-block guard the real `list` rule has, so silent "a list starts here" can disagree with the non-silent rule
union.evidence:
`if (state.sCount[line] < state.blkIndent) return false;` is the only indent check, whereas markdown-it's `list` begins with `if (state.sCount[startLine] - state.blkIndent >= 4) return false` (4+ spaces is indented code). For a line indented exactly 4+ past `blkIndent`, `wrappedList` would return `true` in silent mode (claiming the paragraph terminates) while the non-silent `list` refuses and the `code` rule claims the line, splitting `foo\n -` into `

foo

-
` instead of a lazy continuation. In the stock pipeline this is masked because both `paragraph` and the replaced `lheading` `continue` past lines with `sCount - blkIndent > 3` before invoking terminator rules, so I could not find a reachable trigger — but any other consumer of `getRules('paragraph')` that lacks that skip would hit it. Mirroring the `>= 4` check in `isEmptyBulletLine` makes silent and non-silent agree unconditionally.

union.summary: Re-implemented `asciiTrim` diverges from the upstream rule's `String.prototype.trim()`, so setext heading content keeps non-ASCII whitespace
union.evidence: `return str.replace(ASCII_TRIM_RE, '');` with `ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g`. markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs` uses `state.getLines(...).trim()`, and JS `trim()` also removes U+00A0, U+2028/9, U+FEFF and other Unicode whitespace. So `Heading \n===` yields heading content `"Heading "` here but `"Heading"` upstream — the comment claiming this mirrors "markdown-it's own `asciiTrim`" appears to be inaccurate. Low blast radius (cosmetic), but it is an unintended behavior delta in a rule advertised as a faithful copy.

union.summary: Fix only covers bullet markers; an empty nested *ordered* item (`- 1\n  1.`) still renders as literal lazy text, so the stated "intuitive empty nested item" behavior is inconsistent
union.evidence:
`if (marker !== DASH && marker !== 0x2a && marker !== 0x2b) return false;` — `isEmptyBulletLine` never recognizes ordered markers (`1.`, `1)`), and CommonMark's "empty item cannot interrupt a paragraph" guard applies to ordered lists too. Typing `- 1` then an empty nested `1.` therefore still produces lazy `1
1.` text rather than a nested empty item, i.e. the same class of surprise #517 was filed for is only half fixed. No test in preview.test.ts covers an ordered empty nested item.

union.summary: Single-dash setext H2 (`Title\n-`) now renders as a paragraph plus a stray empty bullet, everywhere in the preview — not just inside a list item
union.evidence:
`lheadingRule` rejects every underline where `marker === DASH && runLength === 1` (line 106), and the wrapped `list` then reports the same line as a paragraph terminator (lines 183-191) with no requirement that the line be *indented into a list item* (`isEmptyBulletLine` only checks `sCount >= blkIndent`, line 32, which is trivially true at top level with blkIndent 0). Trace of `Heading\n-`: lheading declines (isLoneDash), paragraph rule's terminator loop calls wrappedList → true → paragraph ends at line 1, then the non-silent `list` rule matches `-` and emits `
`. Result `

Heading

` where markdown-it/CommonMark/GitHub all give `

Heading

`. This contradicts the doc added in this same change (docs/design/notes/notes.md: "Multi-dash `---` and `=` setext underlines are untouched, so ordinary setext headings still render") — single-dash setext is an ordinary setext heading and it is broken. The change's own TODO lists a "top-level lone dash" test case (docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-todo.md) but preview.test.ts adds none, so the regression is unobserved. Existing notes using `Title\n-` will re-render wrongly.

union.summary: The deviation is widened to `*` and `+` empty bullets, where no setext ambiguity exists, changing rendering of prose lines that are a lone `*`/`+`
union.evidence:
`isEmptyBulletLine` accepts `marker !== DASH && marker !== 0x2a /* * */ && marker !== 0x2b /* + */` → returns false only for other chars, i.e. `*` and `+` empty bullets are also allowed to interrupt a paragraph (wrapper at lines 183-191). The stated rationale ("a lone single `-` is the empty-bullet shape that lheading swallows") does not apply to `*`/`+`: there is no setext underline made of `*`/`+`, and CommonMark deliberately specifies `foo *` → `

foo *

` (spec: "in order for a list to interrupt a paragraph it must start with a non-blank line"). After this change `foo *` and `foo +` render as a paragraph followed by an empty `
`. Only the `-` case is documented/tested, so this extra behavior change is silent.

union.summary: `isEmptyBulletLine` omits the `sCount - blkIndent >= 4` code-block guard that the real `list` rule has, so the wrapper can promise a list the non-silent pass will not build
union.evidence: markdown-it's `list` rule begins with `if (state.sCount[startLine] - state.blkIndent >= 4) return false` (indented code block). `isEmptyBulletLine` only checks `state.sCount[line] < state.blkIndent` (line 32), so for a deeply indented empty bullet (e.g. `- 1\n      -`, sCount 6 with blkIndent 2) the wrapper returns `true` in silent mode, terminating the paragraph, but the subsequent non-silent pass is claimed by the `code` rule instead → an indented code block containing `-` appears where markdown-it previously produced lazy-continuation text `1\n-`. Mitigating factor (why confidence is low): both `paragraph.mjs` and the new `lheadingRule` skip lines with `sCount - blkIndent > 3` before running terminator rules (line 87 here), so the only known callers with `parentType === 'paragraph'` may never present such a line. The guard is still asymmetric with the rule it stands in for, and any other rule/plugin that sets `parentType = 'paragraph'` without that skip reaches it.

union.summary: `list`'s `alt` chain is re-declared from a hardcoded literal instead of being read back from the existing rule entry, silently dropping any membership added by another plugin or a markdown-it version bump
union.evidence: `md.block.ruler.at('list', wrappedList, { alt: ['paragraph', 'reference', 'blockquote'] })` (lines 198-200). `Ruler.at` does `this.__rules__[index].alt = opt.alt || []`, so whatever the entry's alt was is overwritten. `getRuleFn` already reads the private `__rules__` entry (line 208+) and could have copied `rule.alt`; hardcoding means that if any earlier `md.use(...)` in preview.ts (e.g. `detailsPlugin`, applied before this plugin at preview.ts:46) or a future markdown-it release adds a chain to `list`, `list` silently stops terminating that construct. Failure mode is quiet mis-parsing, not an error.

union.summary: `getRuleFn` throws from a module-scope `md.use(...)`, so a markdown-it internals change turns a degraded-rendering bug into a hard module-load failure for the whole notes preview
union.evidence: `if (!rule) throw new Error('markdown-it block rule not found: ' + name)` reads the private `__rules__` registry. `listEmptyBulletPlugin` is invoked at module evaluation time (`md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` at preview.ts:47, top-level of the module), so if markdown-it ever renames/reshapes `__rules__` the throw escapes during import of preview.ts and the notes preview module fails to load entirely (blank/broken editor) rather than falling back to stock rendering. There is no try/catch or feature-detect fallback.

union.summary: Replicated `lheading` uses ASCII-only trimming where upstream uses `String.prototype.trim()`, a second undocumented divergence in a rule that claims to differ by "a single added guard"
union.evidence: upstream markdown-it 14.x lheading does `state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, state.blkIndent, false).trim()`; this copy uses `asciiTrim(...)` (lines 21-23, 135-137), which only strips \t\n\v\f\r and space. Heading text with leading/trailing Unicode whitespace (NBSP U+00A0, U+2003, BOM) is therefore no longer trimmed, e.g. ` Heading\n===` keeps the NBSP inside the `<h1>` inline content. The header comment states the rule "Mirrors the upstream rule ... with a single added guard on the dash run length" (lines 68-69), which is inaccurate.
